content.title: 530A (Trump) Accounts vs. Texas 529 Plans: A quick comparison
content.text: 2-minute read When it comes to planning for your child’s future, two options are making headlines: 530A accounts, commonly known as Trump accounts, and Texas 529 plans. Both aim to help families build financial security, but they serve different purposes. Here’s what you need to know before deciding which is right for you. Origins & Purpose Trump accounts were introduced under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (2025) and are designed to help children build long-term wealth—think of them as a starter retirement account. Texas 529 plans are education-focused savings plans to help families save for college, K–12 tuition, and even student loans. A Texas 529 lets you invest now and withdraw tax-free later towards tuition expenses. Eligibility & Seeding Trump Accounts: Any child under 18 is eligible for a Trump Account but children born between January 1, 2025 and December 31, 2028 qualify for $1,000 government seed into the account. Texas 529 plans: Anyone can open one for a beneficiary without age restrictions. Example: A grandparent can start a Texas 529 for a 10-year-old and begin contributing immediately. Contribution Limits Trump Account: $5,000 per year (plus employer contributions within the cap). Texas 529: Up to $10,000 annually until you reach the $370,000 lifetime cap. Investment Options Trump Accounts are limited to U.S. stock index funds. For example, you can invest your child’s account S&P 500 index fund, but no bonds or international stocks are permitted. Texas 529 plans offer a wide range of portfolios, including age-based options that automatically adjust as your child nears college. Tax Treatment & Withdrawals Trump Accounts provide tax-deferred growth where withdrawals are taxed like a traditional retirement account. Certain uses, like a first home purchase, are penalty-free but taxed as income. Texas 529 plans also offer tax-free growth and withdrawals are generally non-taxable for qualified education expenses. Both Trump Accounts and Texas 529 plans offer unique advantages, but they serve different goals. If your priority is building long-term wealth and giving your child a financial head start, a Trump Account may be the right fit. If education savings and tax-free withdrawals for tuition are your focus, a Texas 529 plan is hard to beat. For many families, a blended approach—contributing to both—can provide the best of both worlds: funding for education today and financial security for tomorrow. The key is understanding your goals and choosing the strategy that aligns with your family’s future.
